speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: asked the Minister for Manpower whether the CPF interest rate will be increased for the next few years to compensate for the high inflation rate that is expected to last for a considerable period, so as to strengthen the retirement adequacy of Singaporeans and seniors.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: asked the Minister for Manpower in computing the CPF Ordinary Account interest rate based on the three-month average of major local banks' interest rates (a) which are the banks identified as major local banks and what are the criteria for selection; (b) what are the types of interest rates and parameters used in the determination; and (c) whether there has been a change in the banks or interest rate parameters used since the formula was introduced.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Ordinary Account (OA) savings is in a liquid account that can be withdrawn at any time for home purchases, for servicing mortgage loans or other specified purposes, such as investments.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Are you taking Question Nos 9 and 10 together?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Sorry, that switch from energy to CPF is quite a significant switch!

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Can I take Question Nos 9 and 10 together, please?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: These three banks have a larger share of domestic deposits than other banks.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This was done to reflect the longer duration that CPF OA monies remained with CPF Board.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As stated in the CPF Board's press release in May 2022, which announced the CPF interest rates effective from July to September 2022, the local banks' three-month average interest rate was 0.09%.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Based on our latest estimates, the interest rate remains at around 0.09%.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The Special, MediSave and Retirement Account, or SMRA, interest rates are pegged to the 12-month average yield of 10-year Singapore Government Securities plus 1%.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The peg was 2.72% as stated in CPF Board's May press release.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: It is around 3%, based on our latest estimates.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: CPF Board will announce in September 2022 the CPF interest rates effective from October to December 2022.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The Government has maintained the floor rate of 4% for the SMRA since 2008 and we will continue to review this on an annual basis.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Therefore, despite the low interest rate environment since the Global Financial Crisis, the Government has continued to pay generous interest rates due to the floor rates.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: If the pegged rates exceed the floor rates, members will correspondingly earn the higher interest rates on their CPF savings.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: There is some time-lag in CPF interest rate adjustments to avoid subjecting members to unnecessary fluctuations.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Members with HDB concessionary loans who pay the prevailing OA interest rate plus 0.1 percentage point also benefit from the stability vis-à-vis the market mortgage rates.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This is the case when interest rates are rising, but the converse also applies when interest rates are falling.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Members can also transfer their OA monies to the Special or Retirement Account to earn the higher, risk-free rate.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I want to emphasise that this is risk-free.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We will continue to review CPF interest rates periodically.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The interest rates on the Ordinary Account, Special Account and MediSave Account are reviewed quarterly, every three months, while the interest rate on the Retirement Account is reviewed annually.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The first is in relation to Member Henry Kwek's question, in terms of the extra interest that can be granted, especially in the inflationary environment.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I note that if you look at the CPF monies, they are invested in special SGS Securities and, basically, these earn for the CPF Board a coupon rate that is pegged to CPF interest rates that members receive.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: If you look over the last 20 years, I think the GIC portfolio nominal returns were about 7% per year.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: So, what will be the hurdle for the Government to consider granting extra interest rates, as it has done from January 2008 and 2016?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The second supplementary question is in relation to the formula which Minister shared that was changed in July 1999.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: It has been more than 20 years since.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I was wondering whether the Government would consider reviewing this formula.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Because, even if you look within the fixed deposits and savings rates for the banks, I just had a look last night – just for DBS, for example, if you look at the 12-month deposit rate, for balances of $20,000 to $50,000, it is 0.05% which is indicated on the CPF Board's website.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: But for less than $20,000, the amount for a 12-month deposit rate would be 1.15% instead.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: And I think over the last few days, the various local banks have also raised their interest rates for their savings accounts, such as the Multiplier and so on.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: So, whether or not these changes in the account types would prompt the CPF Board to review its pegging of the formula?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Many of the policies are decided with input from an Advisory Panel and a Board as well.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The CPF system is aimed at giving members over the longer horizon better security in retirement and old age.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think what the Member was alluding to, in terms of all of these bank accounts, Multiplier accounts and so on, these are very short-term, volatile instruments.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I do not want to belabour the point and take up too much time to go into an extended discussion on this thing.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Like I said, the emphasis is really on long term.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For us, in being custodians of members' monies, we take a very long-term view in providing members with a fair rate of return.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The CPF interest rates, I want to re-emphasise, continue to be attractive.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Members can also transfer their Ordinary Account monies to the Special or Retirement Account to earn the higher interest rate.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And I want to emphasis on this again – the interest rate is risk-free.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think that really tells you how secure your savings are.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The pegged rates have been below 4% since the Global Financial Crisis.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, we are looking at about a 14-year horizon when the peg was introduced.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And again, I want to emphasise to the hon Member, Mr Louis Chua, that this is risk-free.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, I think that the rates that are chosen, these are effective rates, basic rates with no further conditions.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: What the Member was talking about earlier on, in terms of the banks' promotional deposit rates, they are contingent on customers providing fresh funds, or they are only valid for a limited period or for limited amounts of deposits.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Let us take, for example, the DBS Multiplier account.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The bonus interest rates are typically contingent on customers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: If you look at the promotional materials and read the fine print, they are contingent on customers fulfilling other criteria, such as spending on credit cards or crediting of salary.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The effective interest rate, which is what would impact all of us, may be much lower because the bonus rates are usually kept to a certain amount.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, I think, in other words, as financial advisors, it behoves us to actually be very transparent to all of our clients that these benefits are not uniformly applicable to all balances of all the depositors.
